narrative:
On October 6, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 39.6%, with 1,224 of the 3,090 scheduled matters taken up across 51 judges. This performance reflects a slight decline from the 41.7% hearing rate registered on October 5 (1,362 of 3,264 heard) and remains well below the 46.4% clearance recorded on October 1, closely mirroring the 39.5% rate observed on September 30.

Individual bench productivity showed significant variance across the court. Justice K.S. Hemalekha posted the highest individual clearance, hearing 92 of 116 scheduled cases (79.3%), while Justice V. Srishananda heard 60 of 76 matters (78.9%). Substantial hearing volumes were also processed by Justice S. Vishwajith Shetty, who heard 58 of 112 cases in Hall 21 (51.8%) alongside 47 of 105 in Hall 20 (44.8%), and Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum, who took up 53 of 106 cases in Hall 15 (50.0%). In contrast, the Chief Justice's division bench heard none of its 32 scheduled cases, and Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad heard zero cases from an initial list of 113, though clearing 25 of 38 (65.8%) in a separate list.

Procedural conversion rates were strongest in preliminary and procedural stages but declined sharply for final determinations. Preliminary Hearings attained a 49.6% conversion rate (196 of 395), followed by Admissions at 44.2% (382 of 865) and Orders at 41.5% (407 of 980). Conversely, Final Hearings registered a low 19.3% conversion (107 of 553), down from 22.7% on October 5. Across case types, Writ Petitions formed the largest share of the roster, converting 613 of 1,457 scheduled matters (42.1%), down from 48.0% yesterday. Criminal Petitions held steady at 42.9% (213 of 496), while Miscellaneous First Appeals improved to 34.0% (151 of 444) compared to 23.0% on October 5. Regular First Appeals recorded the lowest clearance among major categories at 16.1% (19 of 118).
